ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio; approximately 65% high-intensity (white) pixels to 35% low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white regions occupy the central interior of both lobes; thick black borders along the trailing and lateral edges; a prominent dark vertical band extends from the peduncle to the median notch; irregular black mottling and speckling are concentrated at the color transitions and scattered within the white interior.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel angle of 65 degrees; notch depth extends approximately 15% into the fluke's vertical height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the trailing edge with small micro-peaks; a distinct larger indentation (notch) is visible on the mid-trailing edge of the left lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curve on the lateral leading edges transitioning to a predominantly linear trailing edge with slight upward concavity toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized clusters of high-contrast dark circular spots distributed across the white interiors of both lobes, most notably on the right lobe; small high-intensity white spots are visible on the black trailing edge tips.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple fine, dark, unaligned linear pixel streaks are visible on the white interior surface of the right lobe, oriented diagonally toward the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Visible irregular notch on the trailing edge of the left lobe and multiple smaller nicks along the boundary of both lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: Asymmetrical distribution of focal speckling, with the right lobe showing a higher density of dark points within the white pigmentation compared to the left lobe.
